items.title: Five men arrested in connection with assault with weapons in Petaling Jaya
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Police arrested five men, aged between 30 and 40, on suspicion of being involved in an attack on a man using dangerous weapons at a housing area here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police seized a parang and a saw believed to have been used in the incident. "At 1:03am yesterday, the district police headquarters received a police report from a local man stating that he had been attacked by several people.

items.title: Two women killed in five-vehicle crash in Setiu
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the crash about 4pm. He said initial investigations showed that the Proton Waja travelling from Kota Baru towards Kuala Terengganu was believed to have skidded into the opposite lane before colliding with a trailer lorry. "Following the collision, the trailer also skidded and grazed a Perodua Aruz multi-purpose vehicle, a Perodua Myvi and a UDT lorry travelling from Kota Baru towards Kuala Terengganu," he said in a statement.

items.title: Anthropic AI model sent fake murder tip to Philadelphia police
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police, authorities said Friday, criticising the company for taking two months to report the incident. The Philadelphia Police Department said the false submission was made in July through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a public website where people can share information about unsolved killings. Anthropic's breaches have prompted the White House to mandate that AI companies notify and correct security incidents, news outlet Axios reported citing administration officials.

items.title: Johor extends closure of all schools, religious institutions until Oct 16
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: All schools and educational institutions in Johor, including religious schools, will remain closed for another five days from Monday until Oct 16 due to worsening haze and unhealthy air quality. "The expected wind movement from Kalimantan between Oct 13 and 15 could bring transboundary air pollution, affecting air quality in Johor. Meanwhile, state Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the extended closure also covered Johor Religious Schools, Johor Government Religious Secondary Schools and registered private Islamic education institutions under the Johor Islamic Religious Department (JAINJ).

items.title: Haze: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu open tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual tomorrow as Air Pollutant Index readings in the three states remain under control. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the decision was based on the latest air quality readings. Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed all monitoring stations in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu recorded readings below 100 as of 8pm today.

items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian legislative elections to September next year
items.summary: RAMALLAH, Palestinian Territories: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation over the polls which were last held in 2006. The vote will be held alongside presidential elections on Sept 11, 2027, Abbas said in a decree, blaming "obstacles" imposed by Israel, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency. Israel had blasted Abbas's Palestinian Authority as "corrupt" over the anticipated delay.

items.title: Johari Ghani: Focus of 2027 Budget was to lighten the people's burdens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget was an effort by the government to ease the public's burdens through financial assistance, individual tax relief and tax reductions for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the approach included several measures to help the public cope with daily living expenses while easing the financial burden on workers and businesses. "First, increasing financial assistance to help people purchase goods, supplementing their income with aid provided by the government.

items.title: Fahmi: Don't reshare provocative 3R content, report it to authorities
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said resharing such content would only widen its reach, including by increasing its view count on social media. Fahmi was responding to a social media post by influencer Lim Sian See, whose real name is Datuk Eric Se-To, questioning the use of the word "lighad" in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's speech when tabling the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday. In the post, Lim questioned the word before making a sarcastic association with another word.

items.title: Unauthorised oil blending could tarnish Malaysia’s global image, experts warn
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Oil blending activities must obtain written approval from the Customs director-general where required under the relevant regulations, and be backed by complete documentation to ensure legal compliance and transparent transactions, an expert said. Maritime, Customs and cross-border trade policy and law expert Madzli Harun said every activity involving the import, storage, blending and re-export of oil must be carried out within the scope of the licence and the conditions set by the authorities. Madzli said incomplete documentation, or discrepancies between records and the actual condition of the cargo, could raise questions over the declaration of goods, regulatory compliance and tax treatment.

items.title: Better roads, stronger pitch: MB sees Budget 2027 lifting Negeri Sembilan’s investment appeal
items.summary: Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the construction of a new road from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Bandar Enstek was among the key infrastructure facilities that would support development in the area, while facilitating movement and improving accessibility. “Alhamdulillah, Negeri Sembilan is not being left behind in benefiting from Budget 2027 announced yesterday. The new road will also complement the development of MVV 2.0.

items.title: Saifuddin: Investigation into MCBA chief Shuhaily over KLIA incident ongoing
items.summary: KULIM: Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail is leaving things entirely to the relevant agencies to investigate allegations of assault against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain. The home minister said the probe into the incident where Shuhaily was alleged to have assaulted two Special Branch policemen were continuing after the investigation paper (IP) was returned to police by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC). He said the IP contained witness statements and other evidence.

items.title: Anwar: Budget 2027 will balance fiscal discipline with cost-of-living relief
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — The government will continue to focus on prudent fiscal management in Budget 2027 to return benefits to the people and reduce cost-of-living pressures, especially for low-income households, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, also the finance minister, said although Malaysia’s inflation rate is around two per cent, one of the lowest in the world, the public still feels cost-of-living pressures due to rising prices of goods and certain services. Anwar said the government’s fiscal space has improved through more disciplined financial management, but these savings must be safeguarded from erosion by leakages and waste.

items.title: Anwar says reduced waste and leakages created room for more Budget 2027 aid
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Budget 2027 is the result of good national financial management, with the savings achieved now being returned to the people rather than enjoyed only by certain groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had to resolve the country’s financial priorities first before gaining a greater capacity to channel savings to the people. Anwar said good governance practices allowed the government to provide various forms of assistance and initiatives to the people, including the provision of sports shoes and aid for rubber smallholders and padi farmers.

items.title: 2027 Budget a government pledge to the people, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget represents a "waad" (covenant) or pledge between the nation, its leaders and the people, which must be fulfilled with integrity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the 2027 Budget, the fifth under the unity government, was drawn up by a large team from the Finance Ministry and other ministries, taking into account the needs of various segments of society, from driving economic growth to addressing issues involving employment, wages and minimum income. Anwar said the Madani government had considered the needs of all levels of society when formulating the 2027 Budget, with the aim of elevating the dignity and well-being of the people.

items.title: Budget 2027 more than numbers, says Anwar — it is a promise to the people
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that Budget 2027 is a covenant between the country and its leadership and the people, which must be implemented with full trust and integrity. The finance minister said the Fifth Madani Budget, formulated by a large team under the Ministry of Finance and other ministries, took into account the needs of various segments of society, ranging from driving economic growth to addressing issues concerning employment, wages and minimum income “We want to remind all Malaysians from various walks of life that this budget is not merely about managing finances, but must be an agreement bound by a covenant. “This means a promise, pledge or oath between the country, its leadership and the people.

items.title: 2027 Budget savings to ease cost-of-living pressures, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government will continue to prioritise prudent fiscal management under the 2027 Budget to channel savings back to the people and ease cost-of-living pressures, particularly among lower-income groups. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said savings generated through improved governance and efforts to curb leakages would be channelled back to the people, as the government sought to strengthen the country's finances without compromising assistance for those in need. This approach was important to ensure every ringgit spent by the government delivered greater economic and social value to the people, he said.

items.title: 2027 Budget aims to improve quality of life, ensure social justice for all, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget is designed to ensure a better quality of life and social justice for all Malaysians through a development approach that takes into account the needs of different groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government was not focused solely on headline figures and strategic sectors, but was also looking at the everyday needs of the people, including pet owners, persons with disabilities (PwD), gig workers and food and goods delivery riders. However, Anwar said the 2027 Budget was not intended to solve every problem, but represented steps taken by the government to ease the burden on the people.

items.title: Special task force to probe RM350,000 bribe claims against MACC officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has formed a special task force to review and reexamine allegations of corruption involving RM350,000 linked to a senior officer of the commission. However, following calls for action and the renewed circulation of the claims, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman ordered the immediate establishment of the special task force. "This measure was taken to ensure that the MACC's integrity is upheld and to maintain public confidence in the commission," MACC said in a statement.

items.title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
items.summary: LIMA: Businessman Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores, who shares two of his names with notorious European dictators, has been elected the mayor of a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, according to local election data. The candidate from the left-wing Ahora Nacion party obtained 229 votes out of a total of 663 votes in elections on October 4, according to the National Office of Electoral Processes. In 2021, Peru elected physician Hitler Saavedra Casternoque to parliament for the centrist party Somos Peru.

items.title: Jalaluddin denies plans for no-confidence motion against Negri Sembilan MB
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Jalaluddin Alias has denied plans to submit a motion of no confidence against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim at the upcoming state legislative assembly sitting. The denial follows media reports quoting sources claiming Negri Sembilan Umno was considering the motion, subject to approval from the party's central leadership. Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on Aug 2 following the state election which saw Barisan Nasional win 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11, and Perikatan Nasional seven.

items.title: 2027 Budget balances cost-of-living relief with future growth
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The 2027 Budget strikes a balance between helping Malaysians cope with the rising cost of living and planning for the country's future economic growth, says Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Yusof Apdal. Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a federal allocation of RM18.7 billion for Sabah, up from RM17.6 billion in 2026. Earlier, in his speech, Yusof, a former deputy higher education minister, urged the media to explain the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan facilities announced in 2027 Budget to encourage Sabah students to pursue university education.

items.title: Melaka tourist spots remain busy despite unhealthy API readings
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 10 — Tourist spots around Banda Hilir here continue to draw local and foreign visitors despite Melaka recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings since Thursday due to the haze. A Bernama check at the Stadthuys and Jonker Walk found that tourists were still visiting the popular attractions, while souvenir and handicraft shops remained open as usual. Asmah Zulkifli, 66, from Kuala Lumpur, said the haze had not deterred her and several friends from visiting tourist attractions, including the Stadthuys, after attending a friend’s wedding reception in Bukit Katil here.

items.title: Grieving mother haunted by memories of her three children killed in Pontian accident
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The mother of the three siblings who tragically died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong here, admits that she still finds it difficult to look at her children’s clothes and school bags as they serve as painful reminders of them. Julaiha Munaji, 44, said the simultaneous loss of Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha Norlizan, 8, is the heaviest trial she and her family have ever faced. “I have six children, five boys and one girl.

items.title: Camera traps installed in Fraser's Hill to track tiger spotted there
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Pahang Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has installed four camera traps after receiving reports of a Malayan tiger roaming by the roadside along the Fraser's Hill route near Raub. Pahang Perhilitan director Yusoff Shariff said his department received information regarding the incident about 9am yesterday. "Four Perhilitan officers went to the location to conduct an investigation and install camera traps," he said when contacted.

items.title: 2027 Budget described as 'SME Budget'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) has described the 2027 Budget as an "SME Budget". Samenta president Datuk William Ng said the budget placed micro, small and medium enterprises at the forefront of the nation's economic momentum. He said the financing package and tax cut would provide direct cash flow relief and help businesses address core operating overheads.

items.title: KL Car Free Morning cancelled due to haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Car Free Morning (KLCFM) programme, scheduled to take place at Dataran DBKL here tomorrow, has been cancelled due to the haze. The KLCFM Working Committee said the decision was made after taking into account the risks participants could face from haze exposure, particularly while engaging in outdoor physical activities. "The event scheduled for Sunday, Oct 11, at Dataran DBKL has been cancelled.

items.title: DPM Zahid wants tahfiz graduates equipped for careers in technology, engineering and medicine
items.summary: BANGI, Oct 10 — Tahfiz graduates should have wider opportunities to pursue higher education and professional careers in fields such as technology, engineering and medicine to meet the country’s evolving workforce needs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said tahfiz education should go beyond Quran memorisation by equipping graduates with the knowledge, skills and qualifications needed to pursue a broader range of careers. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts to strengthen tahfiz education included enhancing the National Tahfiz Education Policy, developing the Malaysian Tahfiz Recognition Standard and strengthening pathways through the Malaysian Tahfiz Certificate to broaden graduates’ education and career options.

items.title: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
items.summary: The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this is, however, subject to further directives from the Education Ministry and relevant authorities. "The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual," the statement said. The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Hospital outsourcing scheme to cover more patients, specialities
items.summary: Its deputy director-general of health (medical), Datuk Dr Mohd Azman Yaacob, said the additional RM56 million would enable the ministry to refer more patients to private hospitals for treatment. "HSOP aims to reduce waiting times and ease congestion at government hospitals. "We will increase the number of patients who can receive treatment at private hospitals and explore expanding the programme to other specialities," he said.

items.title: Air quality acceptable for now, Kedah schools to open as usual tomorrow
items.summary: The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this was, however, subject to any further directives from the Ministry of Education and the relevant authorities. “The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual,” the statement said. The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.

items.title: El-Sisi invites Sultan Ibrahim, Anwar to visit Egypt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt. The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today. El-Sisi also touched on cooperation with Malaysia in key areas including energy and renewable energy, manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, and food industries.

items.title: Lights on: Works Department to extend streetlight operating hours during haze
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The Public Works Department (JKR) will extend the operating hours of its streetlights by up to two hours during haze conditions to help improve visibility for road users. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the measure, implemented through JKR’s Electrical Engineering Branch, was prompted by haze conditions that had reduced visibility and increased the risk of accidents. During haze conditions, the operating hours can be extended by up to two hours.

items.title: Teenager drowns at Kuantan beach
items.summary: KUANTAN: A trip to the beach turned tragic when a 16-year-old boy drowned at Pantai Sepat along Jalan Kuantan-Pekan here today. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the body Mohamad Raiyan Khairul Anuar was found about 50m from where he was last seen in the water. "Four divers from the department's Water Rescue Unit in Kuantan and Pekan were later deployed to assist in the search.

items.title: Haze: 28 areas nationwide record unhealthy air quality at 5pm
items.summary: According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, followed by four in Selangor. In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 169, while Batu Muda recorded 160. Putrajaya recorded 161.

items.title: El-Sisi departs after 2-day state visit to Malaysia
items.summary: SEPANG: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin were present to bid farewell to the Egyptian leader. Malaysia's exports to Egypt amounted to RM2.55 billion (US$600 million), while imports totalled RM530 million (US$120 million).

items.title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to prioritise mental health in World Mental Health Day post
items.summary: He said mental health should be cared for alongside physical health, particularly when dealing with the demands of work, family and everyday life. “In the midst of busy work, family and daily life, do not forget to look after our mental health just as we look after our physical health,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with World Mental Health Day today. World Mental Health Day is observed on October 10 every year to raise public awareness of the importance of mental health worldwide.

items.title: Black river waters, dead fish leave Raub villagers worried
items.summary: RAUB: Frustration is mounting among villagers in Kampung Sungai Pasu after Sungai Gali, a popular fishing spot, turned black and began emitting a foul smell. Various species of dead fish have been spotted floating downstream, raising fears of serious water pollution. Sungai Pasu village headman Mohd Zaidi Hashim said the river, which is usually brownish, turned black several days ago, with dead fish floating on the surface.

items.title: Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Turkiye on Saturday formally declared a ban on the use of social media for under-15s, scheduled to come into effect on November 1. It stipulates that social media providers must "take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement" protections for young people. Numerous social media accounts have been blocked in recent weeks.

items.title: Tiger spotted roaming by roadside near Fraser's Hill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malayan tiger was spotted roaming along the road shoulder near Fraser's Hill heading towards Kuala Kubu Baru (KKB), Selangor. According to the post, the tiger was spotted near the GS Gap Chorocco trek area, about one kilometre from the Fraser's Hill junction heading towards KKB. The tiger was spotted roaming by the roadside," the post read.

items.title: India detains 'cockroach' leaders ahead of election protest
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday, the group said, ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission that triggered strict security measures. The demonstration, due to take place in New Delhi, is the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI). Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital, the youth-led CJP said in a social media post, while television networks aired footage showing uniformed police aboard the plane.

items.title: President El-Sisi invites Malaysia’s King, PM to visit Egypt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt. The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today. “It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today.

items.title: Malaysia, Egypt ink four MoUs, strengthen bilateral cooperation
items.summary: The first MoU involved the empowerment of woman, between Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and Egyptian Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Expatriates Minister Dr Badr Ahmed Mohamed Abdelatty. The second, involving higher education, was between Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Abdelatty. For tourism, the MoU was between Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing and Abdelatty.

items.title: Egypt president El-Sisi praises Malaysia for helping injured Gazans, backs Palestinian state
items.summary: He said the Palestinian issue remained central to West Asia and was among the key matters discussed during his meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. El-Sisi also commended Malaysia’s support for the Palestinian people, particularly its humanitarian assistance and efforts to provide medical treatment for injured Palestinians from Gaza. “I would be remiss if I didn't applaud Malaysia's supporting stance regarding the Palestinian issue and its keenness to provide humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian people and also hosting Palestinian second-injured people to get medical care here in Malaysia,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia and Egypt eye easier travel, more business as trade surges, says PM
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will focus on expanding trade and investment cooperation, improving flight connectivity and exploring new areas of economic collaboration at a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting, agreed upon by the two countries’ foreign ministers, would provide a platform to translate growing bilateral ties into broader economic opportunities. He said Malaysia saw considerable potential to expand cooperation with Egypt in several sectors, including semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Health Ministry drafting national registry for persons with disabilities to improve service planning
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through its Family Health Development Division’s Persons with Disabilities (PWD) Sector, has initiated strategic discussions on the development of the MOH PWD Strategic Plan. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was also drafting a proposal for a national-level PWD Registry (OKU Registry), which would incorporate data and needs profiles of the cerebral palsy (CP) community. Speaking to reporters, Dzulkefly said the strategic plan was still at an early stage, but it was important to ensure that the needs of individuals with CP continued to receive attention throughout their lives.

items.title: Eight-metre-deep sinkhole forces closure of Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 10 — The Federal Route FT08 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu Road, near Taman Rekreasi Kesedar here, has been closed to all vehicles today due to a sinkhole measuring about eight metres deep. Road users are advised to use alternative routes via FT2747, namely Jalan Pulai to Bandar Baharu Gua Musang. Meanwhile, Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo, when contacted, confirmed the incident and advised road users to comply with instructions from the authorities.

items.title: Wider electricity bill protection, RM15b National Grid investment will benefit households, says TNB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has welcomed the RM15 billion investment to strengthen the National Grid under Budget 2027, alongside measures to protect domestic electricity consumers and improve energy security. In a statement today, TNB said the investment forms part of its RM43 billion programme from 2025 to 2027 to modernise the country’s electricity infrastructure and meet growing demand. TNB said it would also work more closely with the government to accelerate rural electrification projects, including improvements to electricity supply in Orang Asli settlements, tahfiz and pondok schools.

items.title: Brace for bad weather: Thunderstorms expected in all Malaysian states until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 —The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning, with heavy rain and strong winds expected in Perlis, Kuala Lumpur and 12 other states until 6 pm today. In Perak, the affected areas are Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak and Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai and Jeli, as well as the whole of Terengganu. The same warning has also been issued for Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang, and Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling and Hulu Langat in Selangor.

items.title: Man loses over RM12m in suspected crypto theft
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 10 — A man lost about RM12.47 million after his crypto assets were believed to have been stolen through unauthorised access to his digital wallet. He said the victim realised that a sum of his crypto assets had been transferred out of his digital wallet without his knowledge or consent. “Preliminary investigation found that the transaction involved the transfer of crypto assets through a blockchain network.

items.title: Khazanah backs Budget 2027, pledges support for semiconductor growth and energy transition
items.summary: He said Budget 2027, themed “Malaysia MADANI: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi” , balances economic growth with inclusivity by focusing on strategic sectors such as semiconductors, energy transition, infrastructure, enterprise development and talent development. “Importantly, the Budget places emphasis not only on growth, but on quality growth,” he said. Khazanah also welcomed measures aimed at ensuring broader participation in national development, including initiatives benefiting workers, youth, entrepreneurs, Bumiputera companies, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and communities facing economic and climate-related challenges.

items.title: Egypt president El-Sisi accorded state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara on Saturday on the occasion of his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. Also in attendance were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. Following the welcoming ceremony, El-Sisi inspected a guard of honour comprising 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment.

items.title: Malaysia awaits Indonesia’s response on haze operation as talks continue, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Malaysia is still awaiting a response through official diplomatic channels on arrangements for its offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. Fahmi, who is also the government spokesperson, said discussions had taken place directly between the countries’ leaders and expressed hope that their good relations would allow follow-up action. “I believe that the matter has been conveyed, that discussions have taken place directly with the Indonesian president, and we believe that the good relations today will make it possible for follow-up action to be taken.

items.title: Govt triples Postal Service Fund to RM150m, eyes Q1 2027 rollout to support rural deliveries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government has allocated RM150 million to activate the Postal Service Fund, which is now expected to begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The government has agreed to activate the Postal Fund, which will hopefully begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, with initial funding of RM150 million,” Fahmi told a press conference after officiating the World Post Day celebration at the Pos Malaysia headquarters here today. Fahmi had previously said in January that the government was targeting the fund’s introduction by the third quarter of 2026.

items.title: King confers Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara to El-Sisi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim today consented to the conferring of the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) award to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is currently in Malaysia on a two-day state visit. Also at the ceremony were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, dignitaries, and an Egyptian delegation. Mubarak also undertook an official visit as the Egyptian Vice President in 1979.

items.title: Budget 2027: HKL plans facility upgrades and digital health system rollout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government’s increased allocation for healthcare under Budget 2027 is seen as a catalyst for Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) to upgrade its infrastructure and accelerate its transition to a fully digital hospital. HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K R Nair said the allocation would help the 156-year-old hospital modernise its electrical systems and other facilities, as well as strengthen its information technology infrastructure. This will help us improve facilities for patients.

items.title: Abang Johari appreciates RM16.2b allocation for Sarawak in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 10 — Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg expressed his appreciation to the Madani Government, led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, for the increase in the federal allocation for Sarawak to RM16.2 billion under Budget 2027. “I extend my gratitude to the federal Government for increasing the annual allocation for Sarawak to RM16.2 billion,” he said while speaking at the parade and grand assembly held in conjunction with the 80th birthday celebration of the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, at Padang Merdeka here today. Yesterday, during the Budget 2027 presentation, Anwar announced allocations of RM18.7 billion for Sabah and RM16.2 billion for Sarawak for 2027; in comparison, under the Budget 2026, Sabah received RM17.6 billion while Sarawak obtained RM15.1 billion.

items.title: Paying a carer for your parents or grandparents? Budget 2027 proposes tax relief even for non-medical care
items.summary: Currently, Malaysians can claim a maximum RM8,000 tax relief for spending on these services in Malaysia for their parents and grandparents, who are required to be living in Malaysia: Medical treatment at clinics and hospitals Maximum RM1,000: Full medical examination and vaccinations Dental treatment (excluding cosmetic dental treatment) Treatment and care at home, day care centres and residential care centres Based on existing Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) rules, claims must be supported by the relevant documents, including receipts and medical certification where required: A medical practitioner registered with the Malaysian Dental Council must certify that their medical condition needs dental treatment; A medical practitioner registered with the Malaysian Medical Council must certify that their medical condition needs medical treatment, medical examination or care services. This means that taxpayers currently can only claim for their parents’ or grandparents’ care services if it involves medical care. Yesterday, in Budget 2027, the Finance Ministry proposed that Malaysians be allowed to claim tax relief on “all types of care expenses” for their parents and grandparents at home, day care centres and residential care centres, instead of limiting it to “medical care”.

items.title: Haze sees Malaysian respiratory infections rise 10.43pc, conjunctivitis 26.47pc
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Cases of upper respiratory tract infections rose 10.43 per cent, while conjunctivitis cases increased 26.47 per cent, according to haze-related disease monitoring at 78 selected Health Ministry (MOH) facilities nationwide. In a statement today, the ministry said upper respiratory tract infection cases increased from 3,509 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 39 to 3,875 in EW40, while conjunctivitis cases rose from 102 to 129 over the same period. However, asthma cases fell 13.64 per cent, from 535 to 462.

items.title: API reaches unhealthy levels in 33 areas across Malaysia by 10am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — A total of 33 areas recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 10 am today, with Batu Pahat, Johor, recording the highest reading at 190. Six areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy API readings: Shah Alam (167), Johan Setia (165), Petaling Jaya (161), Klang (157), Banting (154), and Kuala Selangor (152); meanwhile, in Perak, the areas were Tasek Ipoh (174), Pegoh Ipoh (170), Tanjung Malim (168), and Seri Manjung (152). Meanwhile, 35 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at the moderate level.

items.title: Lorry driver tests positive for drugs after ploughing into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam, claims brake failure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The driver of a lorry that crashed into 11 other vehicles at a traffic light junction in Alam Budiman yesterday has tested positive for drugs, police said today. According to Bernama, Shah Alam police chief ACP Sarudin Samah said a urine screening test conducted on the 51-year-old driver found traces of amphetamine and methamphetamine. Preliminary investigations found that the driver claimed to have experienced brake problems while travelling downhill from Puncak Perdana towards Puncak Alam at about 4.20pm.
